# `silk/msgpack/value`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse MessagePack data into an owned tree of values, read fields from it, and write it back.

## When to use
Use [`Msgpack.parse`](#Msgpack.impl.parse) for MessagePack whose shape is not known in advance. Read the tree with
[`Msgpack.field`](#Msgpack.impl.field), [`Msgpack.item`](#Msgpack.impl.item) and the `as` functions such as [`Msgpack.asI64`](#Msgpack.impl.asI64), or by
matching on [`Value`](#Value), and write a tree with [`Msgpack.write`](#Msgpack.impl.write). To read and write your own types, use
`silk.schema.msgpack.SchemaMsgpack`, which builds no tree. To read tokens without allocating,
use `silk.msgpack.scanner.MsgpackScanner`.

## Details
A [`Value`](#Value) owns everything below it. It holds what MessagePack holds and JSON does not: binary
data, extension values, map keys of any kind, and integers up to the largest `u64`. The tree
does not keep the width a number was written in: an integer is [`Value.Integer`](#Value.Integer) when it fits in
`i64` and [`Value.Unsigned`](#Value.Unsigned) above that, and a `float 32` is widened to `f64`. Writing uses the
shortest format for each value, and `float 64` for every float.

## Errors
- `MsgpackError` with a `MsgpackReason` and the byte offset of the problem.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the tree.

## Gotchas
Nesting is limited to 64 levels. Duplicate map keys are kept as written; [`Msgpack.field`](#Msgpack.impl.field)
returns the first. An extension value, such as a timestamp (type -1), is kept as its type and
payload, not interpreted.

## Examples
### Read a field and write the tree back
```silk
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.msgpack.scanner { MsgpackError }
import silk.msgpack.value { Msgpack }

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 32],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, value: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    if self.length + value.length > 32 { fail Writer.failure() }
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, value)
    self.length = self.length + value.length
    return ()
  }

  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! MsgpackError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  // {"port": 8080, "tags": ["a"]}
  let input = b"\x82\xa4port\xcd\x1f\x90\xa4tags\x91\xa1a"
  let document = run Msgpack.parse(input) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let port = Msgpack.field(&document, "port") |> Msgpack.asI64()
  if port.unwrapOr(0) != 8080 {
    return 1
  }
  let mut capture = Capture { bytes: [0; 32], length: 0 }
  run Msgpack.write(&document) |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
  if Slice.view<u8>(&capture.bytes, 0, capture.length) != input {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `Value`

```silk
pub union Value
```

An owned MessagePack value: a scalar, or an array or map that owns its elements.

### Details

An integer is `Integer` when it fits in `i64`, whatever width it was written in, and `Unsigned`
only above the largest `i64`. [`Msgpack.write`](#Msgpack.impl.write) writes either in the shortest format, so a tree
built by hand with a small `Unsigned` writes the same bytes as the `Integer`.

<a id="Msgpack.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Value
    ! MsgpackError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `bytes`, which must be exactly one MessagePack value, into an owned tree.

#### When to use

Use it when the shape of the data is not known in advance. To read a known type, use
`silk.schema.msgpack.SchemaMsgpack.decode`, which builds no tree.

#### Details

Text is checked to be UTF-8 and copied; binary data and extension payloads are copied. An
integer becomes `Value.Integer` when it fits in `i64` and `Value.Unsigned` above that. Map
entries keep their order and are not checked for duplicate keys.

#### Errors

- `MsgpackError` with `UnexpectedEnd` if `bytes` is empty or ends inside the value,
  `ReservedByte` for the byte `0xc1`, `InvalidUtf8` for a string that is not UTF-8,
  `DepthExceeded` if more than 64 arrays and maps are nested, or `TrailingBytes` if bytes
  follow the value. The partial tree is dropped.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the tree.

<a id="Msgpack.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(value: &Value) -> ()
    ! MsgpackError | WriterError
    ? &mut Writer
```

Writes `value` as MessagePack through the ambient `Writer`, without flushing it.

#### Details

Each value is written in the shortest format that holds it, and every float as a `float 64`,
so the bytes of a parsed tree can be shorter than its input, and equal trees write equal
bytes. Map entries are written in their order.

#### Errors

- `MsgpackError` with `MsgpackReason.TooLong` if a string, binary value, extension payload,
  array or map is longer than 4294967295. The values before it stay written.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.

<a id="Msgpack.impl.field"></a>

### Associated function `field`

```silk
pub fn field<'a>(value: &'a Value, key: string) -> Option<&'a Value>
```

Returns the value of the first entry of a map whose key is the text `key`. Returns `None` if
`value` is not a map or has no such key.

#### Details

Only a text key matches: a binary key with the same bytes does not. The returned value
borrows the tree.

<a id="Msgpack.impl.fieldAt"></a>

### Associated function `fieldAt`

```silk
pub fn fieldAt<'a>(value: Option<&'a Value>, key: string) -> Option<&'a Value>
```

Returns the value of the first entry whose key is the text `key` if `value` is a present map.
Returns `None` in other cases.

#### When to use

Use it to read nested fields in a chain:
`Msgpack.field(&document, "user") |> Msgpack.fieldAt("name")`.


Returns the integer that a present `Value.Integer` holds, or `None` for an absent value,
another kind, or a `Value.Unsigned` above the largest `i64`. A float is not converted.

<a id="Msgpack.impl.asU64"></a>

```silk
pub fn asU64(value: Option<&Value>) -> Option<u64>
```

Returns the integer that a present `Value.Unsigned`, or a `Value.Integer` of 0 or more,
holds. Returns `None` for an absent value, another kind, or a negative integer. A float is
not converted.

### Associated function `item`

array or `index` is out of range. The returned value borrows the tree.
